answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked until its actions survive a challenge period; reports from distinct agents count only when backed by separate bonds, and a proven duplicate identity forfeits its bond to the agents who exposed it. This makes creating many identities costly: an attacker must lock up capital for each one and risks losing it, rather than gaining influence by minting free accounts. The umber ledger records claims, basalt marks finalized evidence, and a jetty routes disputes to review.
